textInfo.description: Abhinavagupta's ecstatic nine-stanza devotional anchor. Demonstrates how radical non-dual philosophy transforms into an all-consuming devotional fire where death, fear, and past karma are joyfully surrendered into Bhairava.

verses.devanagari:
व्याप्तचराचरभावविशेषं चिन्मयमेकसन्ततभावम् ।
भैरवनाथमनाथशरण्यं त्वन्मयचित्ततया हृदि वन्दे ॥ १ ॥
verses.iast:
vyāptacarācarabhāvaviśeṣaṃ cinmayamekasantatabhāvam |
bhairavanāthamanāthaśaraṇyaṃ tvanmayacittatayā hṛdi vande || 1 ||
verses.studyGloss: Pervading all moving and unmoving particular states of existence, pure Consciousness itself, undivided and continuous, Lord Bhairava, the sole shelter of the shelterless—I venerate You in my Heart, my mind dissolved in union with You.
verses.practicalContext: Abhinavagupta opens with absolute non-dual devotion: venerating Bhairava not as an external idol, but in the Heart through a mind that has realized identity with Him.

provenance.editionNotes: Encoded by Dott. Marino Faliero, DSO Sanskrit Archive, July 1998.

verses.devanagari:
त्वन्मयमेतदशेषमिदानीं भाति मम त्वदनुग्रहशक्त्या ।
त्वं च महेश सदैव ममात्मा स्वात्ममयं मम तेन समस्तम् ॥ २ ॥
verses.iast:
tvanmayametadaśeṣamidānīṃ bhāti mama tvadanugrahaśaktyā |
tvaṃ ca maheśa sadaiva mamātmā svātmamayaṃ mama tena samastam || 2 ||
verses.studyGloss: Through the power of Your grace, this entire universe now shines before me as Your very being. And You, O Great Lord, are eternally my own innermost Self; therefore, everything in existence is of the nature of my own Self.
verses.practicalContext: The experiential proof of non-dual realization: when God is recognized as one's own Self, the entire universe is cherished as one's own body.

provenance.editionNotes: Encoded by Dott. Marino Faliero, DSO Sanskrit Archive, July 1998.

verses.devanagari:
स्वात्मनि विश्वगते त्वयि नाथे तिष्ठति नित्यमनन्यमयेऽपि ।
सत्स्वपि दुर्धरदुःखविमोहत्रासविधायिषु कर्मगणेषु ॥ ३ ॥
verses.iast:
svātmani viśvagate tvayi nāthe tiṣṭhati nityamananyamaye'pi |
satsvapi durdharaduḥkhavimohatrāsavidhāyiṣu karmagaṇeṣu || 3 ||
verses.studyGloss: When You, the sovereign Lord, eternally abide in my own Self as all-pervading and inseparable, even though masses of difficult karmas cause unbearable grief, delusion, and terror...
verses.practicalContext: Addresses the reality of suffering: karmic storms may rage, but they cannot dislodge the yogi who rests in Bhairava.

provenance.editionNotes: Encoded by Dott. Marino Faliero, DSO Sanskrit Archive, July 1998.

verses.devanagari:
शङ्करसेवनचिन्तनधीरो भीषणभैरवशक्तिमयोऽस्मि ।
भीतिहरं तव पादयुगं तत्सेवितुमद्य दृढोऽस्मि प्रवृत्तः ॥ ४ ॥
verses.iast:
śaṅkarasevanacintanadhīro bhīṣaṇabhairavaśaktimayo'smi |
bhītiharaṃ tava pādayugaṃ tatsevitumadya dṛḍho'smi pravṛttaḥ || 4 ||
verses.studyGloss: Steadfast through contemplation and service of Śaṅkara, I have become embodied with the formidable power of Bhairava. I am resolved to take refuge in Your twin feet, which dissolve all fear.
verses.practicalContext: The non-dual warrior spirit: fear dissolves not by turning away, but by becoming one with the fearless power of Bhairava.

provenance.editionNotes: Encoded by Dott. Marino Faliero, DSO Sanskrit Archive, July 1998.

verses.devanagari:
मृत्युयमान्तककर्मपिशाचैर्नाथ नमोऽस्तु न जातु बिभेमि ।
त्वत्परमामृतवृष्टिसुपूर्णे त्वय्यहमात्मनि निर्वृतिमेमि ॥ ५ ॥
verses.iast:
mṛtyuyamāntakakarmapiśācairnātha namo'stu na jātu bibhemi |
tvatparamāmṛtavṛṣṭisupūrṇe tvayyahamātmani nirvṛtimemi || 5 ||
verses.studyGloss: Salutations to You, O Lord! I no longer have any fear of death, Yama the Lord of Justice, or the ghosts of past karma. Filled to overflowing with the shower of Your supreme nectar, I rest in absolute peace within You, my own Self.
verses.practicalContext: The utter annihilation of existential fear and death-anxiety through immersion in the supreme nectar of consciousness.

provenance.editionNotes: Encoded by Dott. Marino Faliero, DSO Sanskrit Archive, July 1998.

verses.devanagari:
भावपरामृतनिर्भरपूर्णे त्वय्यहमात्मनि निर्वृतिमेमि ।
यत्किञ्चिद्भवतु भवेन्मम नाथ त्वत्पदभक्तिरखण्डितरूपा ॥ ६ ॥
verses.iast:
bhāvaparamṛtanirbharapūrṇe tvayyahamātmani nirvṛtimemi |
yatkiñcidbhavatu bhavenmama nātha tvatpadabhaktirakhaṇḍitarūpā || 6 ||
verses.studyGloss: Resting peacefully in You, my Self, overflowing with the supreme nectar of pure existence, whatever may occur in this worldly life, O Lord, let my devotion to Your feet remain unbroken and complete.
verses.practicalContext: Unbroken devotion in the midst of worldly vicissitudes: whatever life brings, it is welcomed as an expression of divine ecstasy.

provenance.editionNotes: Encoded by Dott. Marino Faliero, DSO Sanskrit Archive, July 1998.

verses.devanagari:
यत्किञ्चिद्भवतु भवेन्मम नाथ त्वत्पदभक्तिरखण्डितरूपा ।
नाथ तदैव मम त्वदभेदस्तोत्रपरामृतवृष्टिरुदेति ॥ ७ ॥
verses.iast:
yatkiñcidbhavatu bhavenmama nātha tvatpadabhaktirakhaṇḍitarūpā |
nātha tadaiva mama tvadabhedastotraparāmṛtavṛṣṭirudeti || 7 ||
verses.studyGloss: O Lord, then alone does the supreme nectar-shower of this hymn of non-difference with You arise spontaneously in my heart.
verses.practicalContext: True praise (stotra) in Kashmir Shaivism is not flattering an external king; it is celebrating the blissful realization of non-difference (abheda).

provenance.editionNotes: Encoded by Dott. Marino Faliero, DSO Sanskrit Archive, July 1998.

verses.devanagari:
तावकशास्त्रपरामृतचिन्ता स्यन्दति चेतसि निर्वृतिधाराम् ।
येन विभुर्भवरुक्परितापं संहरते झटिति प्रथितश्रीः ॥ ८ ॥
verses.iast:
tāvakaśāstraparāmṛtacintā syandati cetasi nirvṛtidhārām |
yena vibhurbhavarukparitāpaṃ saṃharate jhaṭiti prathitaśrīḥ || 8 ||
verses.studyGloss: Contemplation of the supreme nectar of Your sacred teachings pours a river of tranquil bliss into my mind, by which the all-pervading, glorious Lord instantly dissolves the feverish torment of worldly illness.
verses.practicalContext: Philosophical study (śāstra-cintā) as direct medicine: immersing in non-dual philosophy cools the fever of mental agitation.

provenance.editionNotes: Encoded by Dott. Marino Faliero, DSO Sanskrit Archive, July 1998.

verses.devanagari:
त्वां प्रियमप्य सुदर्शनमेकं दुर्लभमन्यजनैः समयज्ञम् ।
येन विभुर्भवमरुसन्तापं शमयति जनस्य झटिति दयालुः ॥ ९ ॥
verses.iast:
tvāṃ priyamapya sudarśanamekaṃ durlabhamanyajanaiḥ samayajñam |
yena vibhurbhavamarusantāpaṃ śamayati janasya jhaṭiti dayāluḥ || 9 ||
verses.studyGloss: Having attained You, the one beloved, radiant and clear to direct sight, hard to reach by ordinary people, the compassionate Lord who knows the secret timing quenches the burning desert-heat of transmigratory existence for all seekers.
verses.practicalContext: The Guru and Lord as the secret wellspring in the desert of saṃsāra, quenching existential thirst.

provenance.editionNotes: Encoded by Dott. Marino Faliero, DSO Sanskrit Archive, July 1998.

verses.devanagari:
समाप्तमिदं स्तवमभिनवाख्यं पद्यनवकम् ।
येन विभुर्भवमरुसन्तापं शमयति जनस्य झटिति दयालुः इति शिवम् ॥ १० ॥
verses.iast:
samāptamidaṃ stavamabhinavākhyaṃ padyanavakam |
yena vibhurbhavamarusantāpaṃ śamayati janasya jhaṭiti dayāluḥ iti śivam || 10 ||
verses.studyGloss: Thus concludes this nine-stanza hymn named Abhinava, through which the compassionate Lord swiftly quenches the burning fever of suffering. All is auspiciousness; all is Śiva.
verses.practicalContext: Abhinavagupta seals the hymn with his own signature ('abhinava') signifying both his lineage name and ever-new awareness.

provenance.editionNotes: Encoded by Dott. Marino Faliero, DSO Sanskrit Archive, July 1998.
